subject: Taxes
title: Revolts That Changed the Law
description: A micro-lesson that makes Revolts That Changed the Law usable.

hook.text: The Magna Carta, the US Constitution, France's Declaration of Rights.

buildup.text: Tax revolts don't just lower rates. They create institutions: parliaments, constitutions, and rights of representation.

discovery.text: England's Glorious Revolution of 1688 established that Parliament—not the king—controls taxation.

twist.text: Even failed revolts change law. The Peasants' Revolt failed, but England never imposed a poll tax for 600 years.

climax.text: Tax revolts are the engine of democratic progress. The right to consent to taxation built the modern state.

punchline.text: Every great constitution began with a tax revolt. No exception.

quiz.question: What did England's 1688 Glorious Revolution establish about taxation?
options: Parliament, not the king, controls taxation
